items.informal_name: Equivalence of Universal Quantification over Binary Image and Original Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} {f : α → β → γ} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {p : γ → Prop},
  (∀ (z : γ), z ∈ Set.image2 f s t → p z) ↔ ∀ (x : α), x ∈ s → ∀ (y : β), y ∈ t → p (f x y)
items.informal_description: For any property $ p : \gamma \to \Prop $, the statement that $ p(z) $ holds for all $ z $ in the image of $ f $ on $ s \times t $ is equivalent to $ p(f(x, y)) $ holding for all $ x \in s $ and $ y \in t $. Formally, $ \forall z \in \mathrm{image}_2(f, s, t),\, p(z) $ if and only if $ \forall x \in s, \forall y \in t,\, p(f(x, y)) $.

items.informal_name: Equivalence of Universal Quantification over Binary Image and Original Sets
items.type:

  {p : γ → Prop}, (∀ z ∈ Finset.image₂ f s t, p z) ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, p (f x y)
items.informal_description: For any property $ p $ on $ \gamma $, the statement that $ p(z) $ holds for all $ z $ in the image of the binary function $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $ over finite sets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $ is equivalent to the statement that $ p(f(x, y)) $ holds for all $ x \in s $ and $ y \in t $.

items.informal_name: Existence in Image of Binary Function on Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} {f : α → β → γ} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {p : γ → Prop},
  (∃ z, z ∈ Set.image2 f s t ∧ p z) ↔ ∃ x, x ∈ s ∧ ∃ y, y ∈ t ∧ p (f x y)
items.informal_description: For a binary function $f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma$ and subsets $s \subseteq \alpha$, $t \subseteq \beta$, there exists an element $z$ in the image of $f$ on $s \times t$ satisfying a property $p$ if and only if there exist elements $x \in s$ and $y \in t$ such that $p(f(x, y))$ holds.

items.informal_name: Characterization of Existence in Binary Image of Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β}
  {p : γ → Prop}, (∃ z ∈ Finset.image₂ f s t, p z) ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t, p (f x y)
items.informal_description: For a binary function $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $, finite sets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $, and a predicate $ p : \gamma \to \Prop $, there exists an element $ z \in \mathrm{image}_2(f, s, t) $ such that $ p(z) $ holds if and only if there exist elements $ x \in s $ and $ y \in t $ such that $ p(f(x, y)) $ holds.

items.informal_name: Image of Binary Function is Subset iff All Applications Contained
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} {f : α → β → γ} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {u : Set γ},
  Set.image2 f s t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ (x : α), x ∈ s → ∀ (y : β), y ∈ t → f x y ∈ u
items.informal_description: The image of a binary function $f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma$ on sets $s \subseteq \alpha$ and $t \subseteq \beta$ is a subset of $u \subseteq \gamma$ if and only if for all $x \in s$ and $y \in t$, the value $f(x, y)$ is an element of $u$. Formally, $\{c \in \gamma \mid \exists a \in s, \exists b \in t, f(a, b) = c\} \subseteq u$ is equivalent to $\forall x \in s, \forall y \in t, f(x, y) \in u$.
